text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated GPU pool 'dedicated-enterprise-eu' CPU/GPU allocation at 100% and autoscaler health degraded. queue_length=842, avg_latency_tokens=1.8s, scale_attempts=5
Mia Chen: I'm on it. Paging infra-oncall and Samir. Looks like reserved GPUs fully utilized for the enterprise pool.
Samir (oncall): I'm awake. pulling logs now. Can someone confirm which tenants are impacted?
Raj P.: Customer telemetry shows high traffic from tenant 'acme-corp' and several batch jobs from 'datafarm' started at 02:12 UTC. Could be noisy neighbor.
Leah O'Neill: Confirming: alerts from Redwood Console show throttling and queuing on dedicated-enterprise-eu. Several requests are falling back to hosted but that's hitting rate limits.
Infra Oncall: Autoscaler reports unable to provision additional nodes due to pool limit (hard cap reached: 48 GPUs). scale_attempts: 5, last_error: "quota exceeded".
Mia Chen: Can we raise the cap temporarily? Who owns the quota with cloud account? @Anna (acct) can you confirm?
Anna (acct): I see the committed capacity for that pool is 48 GPUs under the Dedicated contract. We have the option to burst to shared pool but need approval from sales/finance. Not immediate.
Samir (oncall): Short-term mitigation ideas: 1) apply temporary per-tenant throttles (rate-limits) 2) evict lower-priority batch work 3) route enterprise traffic to hosted fallback for customers with fallback enabled.
Raj P.: I can start evicting non-urgent batch jobs. Which jobs are safe? Use tag: "dedicated:low-priority".
Leah O'Neill: I'll run a scan and provide a list. Running query: SELECT job_id, tenant, priority FROM jobs WHERE pool='dedicated-enterprise-eu' AND started > now()-3h ORDER BY priority ASC;
eng-sre-bot: Query returned 27 jobs with priority<=5. Potential reclaimed GPUs: ~8.
Mia Chen: Great. Raj, please kill the low-priority jobs and cordon nodes used exclusively by them. Make sure to document in ticket.
Raj P.: Killing jobs now. Commands: 
```
# list low-priority jobs
redwoodctl job list --pool dedicated-enterprise-eu --filter priority<=5 --output json
# cancel
redwoodctl job cancel <job_id>
```
Raj P.: Done. Freed ~6 GPUs but queue still high (now 782).
Samir (oncall): I'm going to enable per-tenant throttling for 'datafarm' and 'acme-corp' to limit concurrency from 20 -> 5. Applying policy.
Mia Chen: Apply a soft-failure policy: for enterprise tenants, allow fallback to hosted with degraded SLA. Notify their account teams.
Anna (acct): Notifying AMs now: pinged @acme-account-team and @datafarm-account. I'll open a customer incident and mark as "service-impacting".
eng-sre-bot: Throttle policy applied: datafarm concurrency=5, acme-corp concurrency=5. Estimated immediate reduction ~40% in active sessions.
Leah O'Neill: After throttles, queue_length=420 and avg_latency_tokens=1.1s. Still above SLO for dedicated tier but improved.
Samir (oncall): Trying one more scale attempt to shared-burst pool. Running autoscaler override: 
```
# attempt burst to shared pool
redwoodctl scale override --pool dedicated-enterprise-eu --burst-to shared-burst-eu --gpus 12
```
Infra Oncall: Override failed: "burst denied: billing_account_locked_for_quota_changes". Need billing/finance unlock.
Mia Chen: OK, fallback plan: proactively route traffic for non-SLA customers to hosted pool and keep enterprise tenants on degraded service. We'll prepare a status update.
Anna (acct): Finance notified and I have escalation in flight (+1 on call with billing). ETA 25m for decision on temporary burst.
Raj P.: While we wait, I'm rebalancing pods to reduce fragmentation across nodes; will pack higher-priority tenants first.
Leah O'Neill: Rebalance done. Reclaimed 3 more GPUs. Queue_length now 312.
Samir (oncall): Reapplied emergency eviction for jobs tagged test/dev that were still running. Freed 2 GPUs. queue=288.
Mia Chen: We're at partial mitigation. Prepare a public-facing incident update: include impact (throttling for enterprise dedicated pool, some requests falling back to hosted, potential increased latency), steps taken, ETA for resolution (waiting on billing). @Anna please include affected customer list in the update.
Anna (acct): Drafting update: "We are experiencing capacity constraints in our Dedicated EU GPU pool impacting some enterprise workloads. We have applied throttles and evicted low-priority batch jobs. Our teams are working to provision temporary burst capacity; expected update in ~25 minutes."
eng-sre-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-0456. Linked PR: #cloud-burst-policy.
Samir (oncall): Handoff note for next oncall (in 45m): we've applied throttles to top noisy tenants, evicted low-priority jobs, attempted burst but blocked by billing. Still monitoring queue and latency. If queue doesn't drop below 100 in next 20m, escalate to Eng Infrastructure and Sales for immediate manual burst.
Mia Chen: I'm staying on for the handoff and will update post-billing decision. Also propose post-incident actions: 1) add an emergency burst role for ops 2) implement pre-approved burst for enterprise SLAs 3) per-tenant circuit-breakers to auto-throttle noisy tenants.
Raj P.: Agreed. I'll capture noisy neighbor fingerprints and build a daily report to detect recurrence.
Leah O'Neill: Monitoring: last metrics snapshot: 
```
queue_length: 288
gpu_utilization: 99.6%
avg_latency_tokens: 1.05s
drop_rate: 0.7%  # requests that failed before fallback
```
Anna (acct): Billing just confirmed temporary unlock for 12 GPUs. Finance requires retrospective approval and cost attribution to enterprise credits. Proceed?
Mia Chen: Proceed. Infra Oncall, please run the scale override again.
Infra Oncall: Running override now...
```
redwoodctl scale override --pool dedicated-enterprise-eu --burst-to shared-burst-eu --gpus 12 --approve-billing
```
eng-sre-bot: Scale override succeeded. 12 GPUs added to pool. New capacity=60 GPUs.
Samir (oncall): Queue draining, queue_length=94, avg_latency_tokens=0.45s. Rolling back throttles in 10m if metrics stable.
Leah O'Neill: Notifying account teams update: capacity increased, performance improving. Will keep them updated on RCA.
Anna (acct): Sent customer updates. Some customers already reported degraded experience in last 3h; offering credits per SLA.
Mia Chen: Incident severity de-escalation check: still open but we've mitigated immediate customer impact. Keeping incident open for RCA, and schedule postmortem.
Samir (oncall): Handoff complete. Next oncall: monitor for 30m, validate that throttles are removed cleanly and no regression.
Mia Chen: Thanks all. Postmortem owners: Samir and Raj. Action items assigned in INC-2026-0456: add pre-approved burst workflow, quota alert to trigger earlier at 85%, tenant circuit-breakers, and noise-detection report. :white_check_mark:
